Why this matters (The Square-Cube Law)
As a sphere grows larger, its volume grows much faster than its surface area. This mathematical reality dictates why biological cells stay tiny (to maximize surface area for absorbing nutrients) and why giant spherical structures hold heat much better than small ones.

1. The "Square" (Surface Area)
The surface area of a sphere relies on the radius squared (
r2r squared
):
Surface Area=4πr2Surface Area equals 4 pi r squared

Because area is a two-dimensional measurement, if you double the radius of a sphere, its surface area increases by a factor of
222 squared
, or 4 times. 
2. The "Cube" (Volume)
The volume of a sphere relies on the radius cubed (
r3r cubed
):
Volume=43πr3Volume equals four-thirds pi r cubed

Because volume is a three-dimensional measurement of space, if you double the radius of a sphere, its total volume increases by a factor of
232 cubed
, or 8 times.
